gloss: heaven · sky · nature — and what is given (天命)
formNote: The Shuowen: 天，顛也。至高無上，从一大 — “the crown of the head; highest, with nothing above; from 一 and 大.” Early forms show a person (大) with a large head; the head is what is highest.
summary: The sky, Heaven, and what is given rather than chosen: Confucius knew the mandate of Heaven at fifty, Zhuangzi heard the piping of Heaven. In the Yijing’s cosmology 天 is the first of the Three Powers, with Earth and the human.
placement: At the tip of the upper lobe. Halvorsen’s system is unchanged when x → y → z, so seen down the line x = y = z it shows three lobes, 120° apart: 天, 地 and 人 take one each, the Three Powers. (Placement is a design choice, not a claim.)

oc.note: † Baracus, from general knowledge; not yet checked against B–S 2014.

satellites.title: The Crown of the Head
satellites.evidence: The Shuowen glosses 天 by a near-homophone, 顛, “the crown of the head”, and adds 至高無上, “highest, with nothing above”. Heaven is first the top of a person, then the top of the world.
satellites.caveat: Glossing by sound (聲訓) is a Han method; it records how the word was understood, not necessarily where it came from.

satellites.title: The Mandate of Heaven
satellites.evidence: Analects 2.4: 五十而知天命 — “at fifty I knew the mandate of Heaven.” 命, “command, fate”, given by 天: what is set for a person, to be understood rather than chosen.
